tecnicas.nome_original: GPT-4o Refined Hint Prompting (GPT-4o refined prompting)
tecnicas.localizador: PDF p. 8 (impressa 473), Seção V.B e Fig. 3; Tabela III e Fig. 4, PDF p. 9 (impressa 474)
tecnicas.observacao: Segunda abordagem do Hint-Driven Prompting. As dicas oficiais e o enunciado são enviados ao GPT-4o, que reescreve a solução como instruções passo a passo de implementação; essas dicas refinadas são fornecidas aos LLMs geradores. Mecanismos: contexto (dica derivada da solução oficial) e decomposicao (plano passo a passo, semelhante a pseudocódigo intermediário), além de instrucao e restricoes herdadas do prompt base. mecanismos_acrescentados em relação à técnica de que deriva (USACO Hint Prompting); em relação ao prompt base seriam contexto e decomposicao. A reescrita é de passo único, sem busca nem retorno de desempenho, por isso não foi classificada como otimizacao_prompt. Contrafactuais na Tabela III: No Hints e USACO Hints, mesmos modelos e mesmos casos.

citacoes.trecho: Through a detailed analysis, we identify common code generation errors across the models and propose Hint-Driven Prompts to address logic errors, alongside the Syntax Mitigation Prompt to reduce syntax bugs.

Our results demonstrate that the Hint-Driven Prompt boosts pass rates for DBRX 132B, Deepseek-Coder 33B, Codegemma 7B, Codellama 7B, Llama3, and GPT-4o by 6.6x, 4.7x, 3x, 2.5x, 2.1x, and 25%, respectively.
To assist LLMs in identifying and correcting logic errors, we propose a Hint-Driven Prompting methodology, which encompasses two approaches: USACO Hint Prompting and GPT-4o Refined Hint Prompting.
However, our crawler removes any code from the solutions, as the goal is to provide hints for LLMs generating correct code rather than adapting pre-written programs.
The GPT-4o is then prompted with the following request: “Put the solution into your own words; do not explain anything prior—just provide the step-by-step instructions on how to implement it.”
Note: This Syntax Mitigation Prompt is given alongside the GPT-4o refined hints for LLMs to generate code.
Additionally, we add in simple Python error examples and variations to ensure that the model doesn't make those errors again.
Specifically, 36.8% of the test cases that fail are due to logic errors in the code generated by LLMs.
Across all 11 LLMs we evaluate, the overall error distribution shows 36.8% logical failures, meaning that the majority of errors stem from code that runs but produces incorrect outcomes.
They also suffer from “data contamination” [19] [20] [21] when problems overlap with LLM training datasets [22], which skews reported performance [23] [24] [25].
First, USACO is less likely to be included in training data compared to other coding platforms like CodeForces, minimizing concerns of benchmark leakage and overfitting [21].
Five models out of 11 models tested were selected to show an overall decrease in syntax bugs, including Deepseek-Coder 33B, Codellama 70B, Codegemma 7B, Llama 3 8B, and GPT-4o.

In the case of Codestral 22B, there is only a marginal improvement with the USACO hints, with test cases passed slightly increasing from 423 to 424, but a drop to 73 test cases following the GPT-4o refined hints which can be explained by a large surge in IndentationError.
The findings of our study may be limited by the relatively small size of the USACO dataset.
